items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: From there I just -- I went to a banjo and I heard Eddie Lang and I made up my mind then that I was going to play guitar.

ctx.x: Did you start on guitar or did you start on banjo?

No, I started on banjo -- I started on the ukulele. I'm getting ahead of my story. Actually, how I started playing a string instrument. My mother gave my sister, who also was a very fine pianist herself, marvelous pianist, she gave her a ukulele. And I took it and played it. My sister never could play it and I just took it and just played it. And this is how I think this is the beginning of the string instrument for me. From there I just -- I went to a banjo and I heard Eddie Lang and I made up my mind then that…

But the thing of it is nobody taught guitar then. You couldn't get a teacher. They -- everybody was groping, they didn't know too much about it themselves, so you just had to have some ingenuity and imagination, I should say, and do
